summary: Relocating engineer (EU) — laptop shipment hold, Okta/SCIM license transfer & local KMS compliance questions
description: Issue summary: New full-time hire (engineer) is relocating from US to Ireland. Shipping partner has flagged package for customs paperwork, Okta/SCIM provisioning did not assign paid JetBrains/VMware seats, and the customer/legal team has asked whether we must use local KMS/HSM for keys when an employee's work touches EU customer data. We need a coordinated plan: get the employee productive with minimum delay, transfer required software licenses, confirm policy for key residency for employee-level dev tooling, and unblock hardware customs.
impact: Employee start-date risk: inability to access paid developer tools (JetBrains, VMware), delay in laptop delivery (estimated 5-10 business days), risk of exposing work to non-compliant key storage if we instruct use of personal encryption. Potential escalation to HR and legal if start is missed.
background: New hire ID: RWI-2026-312 (HR record). Offer accepted with relocation assistance. Laptop (MacBook Pro) shipped from US vendor on 2026-03-08 but is currently held by Dublin customs pending EORI/Commercial invoice clarification. Okta account created on 2026-03-09 via SCIM; however, JetBrains seat not auto-assigned and VMware Workstation license request returned a 'no seat available' message. Legal asked whether an EU-based employee must use EU-located KMS/HSM for any private keys used in their day-to-day work when working on customer data that is EU-resident.
desired_outcome: 1) Clear next steps to release laptop (paperwork checklist and contact at shipping partner). 2) Temporary secure access plan so the engineer can start (cloud dev VM + short-term loaner laptop policy). 3) Perform software license transfer or temporary seat assignment for JetBrains/VMware. 4) Definitive answer from Security/Legal on whether we require country-specific KMS/HSM for engineer dev keys, and guidance on how to onboard the employee securely in the meantime.
steps_taken: - Confirmed Okta user exists and SCIM sync last successful at 2026-03-09T17:12Z. - Opened case with shipping vendor; assigned tracking #EU-778233. - Requested JetBrains/VMware seat pool checks from Licensing Portal (request ID LIC-4921). - Pinged Legal and Security for KMS policy clarification (slack thread #security-compliance).
observed_behavior: - Laptop held by customs due to missing EORI/Commercial invoice details (customs note: 'insufficient paperwork for employer shipment'). - SCIM created Okta account but group memberships did not propagate to the licensing groups used by JetBrains. - Licensing portal shows zero available VMware seats in EU pool; US pool has available seats but cross-region transfer is manual and flagged by finance for billing implications.
logs: Okta SCIM logs (2026-03-09): user provisioned, groups sync attempted => group 'dev-paid-tools' not found in SCIM mapping. Licensing portal export (2026-03-10): VMware pool EU: 0 free seats; US: 3 free seats. Shipping vendor message ID: SV-EU-31872.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Aisha Raman: Adding initial context and HR contact. HR has provided the commercial invoice template; they need confirmation which EIN/EORI fields should be filled by Redwood. HR contact: Maren O'Connell.

2026-03-10 | Diego Morales: I will reach out to the shipping vendor ops and Okta admin team. Immediate ask: can we provision a temporary cloud dev VM (eu-west) with company-managed disk encryption and MFA access so the hire can start?

2026-03-11 | Diego Morales: Shipping vendor responded — they require the employer EORI and the original invoice sender (vendor) to reissue a commercial invoice with recipient VAT. I've requested that HR provide company EORI and a signed commercial invoice template. See slack thread #ops-logistics link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C08SHIPPING/p1623

2026-03-11 | Priya Khatri (Licensing): JetBrains seats: we have 2 floating EU seats but they are assigned to other teams. We can issue a temporary seat for 30 days if Finance approves cross-team seat loan. I'll open LIC-4921 and cc finance. VMware: EU pool is zero; finance flagged cross-charging issues for cross-region assignment.

2026-03-12 | Marcus Le (Security): Regarding KMS/HSM: short answer — personal developer keys used for day-to-day dev tools do not currently require an EU-local HSM under our policy. If the engineer will hold customer production keys or persist customer EU-resident secrets locally, we need to provision keys under EU KMS and follow key-access logging and HSM policy. For onboarding, recommend company-managed cloud VM in eu-west with company KMS keys — avoids local key residency concerns.

2026-03-12 | Diego Morales: Action plan proposed: (A) HR to send EORI/commercial invoice details to shipping vendor (B) IT to provision temporary eu-west cloud VM with preinstalled dev tools and company KMS access (C) Licensing to approve 30-day temporary JetBrains seat and check VMware short-term license or allow remote use of US-licensed VM through VPN. I will start provisioning once HR confirms paperwork.

2026-03-12 | Maren O'Connell (HR): Uploaded signed commercial invoice and company EORI to the shipping vendor portal and confirmed with carrier contact (Davy at ShipFast). Please confirm the exact fields required on the invoice for a company-owned laptop to clear without VAT hold.
next_steps: 1) Diego to provision eu-west cloud VM with company image and KMS access (target: 2026-03-12 EOD). 2) HR to confirm invoice fields and confirm with shipper (target: 2026-03-12). 3) Licensing to approve temporary JetBrains seat and either provide VMware remote license or approve alternate remote dev environment (target: 2026-03-13). 4) Security to provide formal note on KMS residency for HR/Legal (target: 2026-03-13).
